title: Z-Wave Everspring ST814 no longer updates temperature or humidity
body: I am using Z-Wave JS 0.1.34 with Home Assistant Core 2021.8.1 on Home Assistant OS. My Everspring ST814 no longer reports temperature or humidity, although the logs show it waking every hour. When it previously worked, the logs contained a message mapping an unsolicited report from the root device to endpoint 1, but I no longer see that message. Another user has reported the same problem in the Home Assistant community forum.

symptoms_visible: My Everspring ST814 temperature and humidity values no longer update in Home Assistant, even though I see the device wake every hour.
I no longer see the root-device-to-endpoint mapping message that appeared in the logs when updates worked.
N0.label: N0 ST814 values no longer update

symptoms_visible: Automatic temperature and humidity reports still do not update the entities.
Calling refresh on an entity can update it, but the result takes a few minutes to appear.
N1.label: N1 manual refresh behavior established

symptoms_visible: The Z-Wave logs receive temperature and humidity values, but the corresponding Home Assistant entities do not change.
N2.label: N2 report and entity endpoints captured

symptoms_visible: After applying the endpoint-1 mapping override, the temperature entity updates but the humidity entity still does not.
N2_x.label: N2_x endpoint-1-only mapping aftermath

symptoms_visible: Temperature can update with the override, but humidity remains stale even though a humidity report appears in the Z-Wave log.
N3.label: N3 humidity endpoint evidence collected

symptoms_visible: After updating to driver 8.4.1 and server 1.10.7 and re-interviewing the device, the sensor still does not reliably update.
The re-interview leaves multiple temperature and humidity entities, with only one set close to the device's current readings.
N4_x.label: N4_x earlier driver update and re-interview aftermath

symptoms_visible: After setting the report interval to five minutes, I see the setting being received but no temperature or humidity reports arrive.
I removed and re-added the device, and it still sends no reports.
N5_x.label: N5_x re-added device has no reports

symptoms_visible: After updating the Z-Wave JS add-on and re-interviewing the ST814, its temperature and humidity entities update as expected.
N_terminal.label: terminal ST814 updates restored

question_patterns: Do you remember approximately when this last worked, or which Home Assistant and Z-Wave JS versions you had then?
When did the ST814 last update normally?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I cannot recall an exact version. I would say it last worked around two months ago, and I generally keep Home Assistant up to date.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I think it last worked six weeks ago rather than two months ago, but I do not know the exact version.

edges.comment: The reporter initially said refresh made no change, then voluntarily corrected that observation after waiting several minutes. The delayed refresh result is therefore target-node volunteered information rather than a prompted conclusion.

question_patterns: Please re-interview the device with debug logging enabled, manually wake it, and attach the complete log and network dump.
Can you capture a full Z-Wave JS debug log and network dump while the ST814 reports?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I've attached the re-interview log, the network dump, and a separate log containing updates from the ST814. The incoming temperature and humidity lines are marked Endpoint 0, while the dump lists the entity values on endpoints 1 and 2. The values arrive in the log, but my Home Assistant entities do not change.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The full log contains no temperature or humidity report from the device at all, even after I wake it.
The same endpoint numbers appear, but the device has a different node ID.

edges.comment: Logs and dumps were supplied by another affected ST814 owner and are folded into the single simulated user side. The answer preserves raw endpoint labels from the artifacts; interpreting their mismatch as the cause is engineer-side.

solution.intent: participant81 the ST814 device configuration so unsolicited root reports are mapped to endpoint 1, then reload the configuration and re-interview the device.
solution.concrete_example: Add the endpoint-1 compatibility mapping to the ST814 configuration, reload the driver configuration, and re-interview the battery device.

edges.comment: This exact initial configuration direction was tested in zwavejs2mqtt. It restored temperature updates but not humidity, so endpoint-1-only mapping is a known incomplete path.

question_patterns: Can you capture and paste the raw log lines for an incoming humidity report?
What does the full Z-Wave log print when the device sends humidity?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The humidity report says Endpoint 0 with value 54, followed by 'Mapping unsolicited report from root device to endpoint #1' and another humidity value line for Endpoint 1. The entity still does not update.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The humidity report is already multi-channel encapsulated for endpoint 2 and the endpoint-2 entity updates normally.

edges.comment: The raw humidity report came from another affected owner and is folded into the simulated user side. The observation that the dump exposes humidity on endpoint 2 was volunteered alongside the requested log.

solution.intent: Install the available Z-Wave JS driver update containing the ST814 device-configuration change and re-interview the sensor.
solution.concrete_example: Update the Z-Wave JS add-on or server to a driver release containing the ST814 configuration update, then wake and re-interview the device so its values are recreated.

edges.comment: Affected users installed driver 8.4.1/server 1.10.7 and re-interviewed. The issue was not reliably resolved and the device exposed extraneous endpoint values, so this earlier update alone is a known blind path.

solution.intent: Remove and re-add the ST814 after shortening its reporting interval, then re-interview it to recreate the device and entities.
solution.concrete_example: Set the ST814 reporting interval to five minutes, remove and include it again, and run another interview while collecting the log.

edges.comment: The reporter tried this persistent device change independently. The five-minute setting was accepted, but reports stopped entirely; the attached interview log printed that the lifeline could not be assigned.

solution.intent: Update the Z-Wave JS add-on to a build containing both the corrected ST814 root-value compatibility handling and the association setup correction, then re-interview the node and verify that both sensor entities update.
solution.concrete_example: The issue was confirmed resolved after updating the Home Assistant Z-Wave JS add-on to 0.1.46, which used node-zwave-js 8.7.5 and server 1.10.8, and then re-interviewing the ST814 devices.
solution.inference_hint: Engineers inferred two related driver-side failures from the raw artifacts: the ST814 sends unencapsulated temperature and humidity reports from endpoint 0 while its generated entity values were exposed on endpoints 1 and 2, and after reinclusion the failed group-1 lifeline assignment prevented unsolicited reports entirely. The reporter supplied endpoint-labelled logs and the failed-assignment line but did not formulate those conclusions.

edges.comment: Final resolution from the thread tail: after a newer Z-Wave JS add-on incorporated the relevant driver corrections, affected users re-interviewed their ST814 devices and confirmed that both values updated normally.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause from the collected artifacts: the ST814 sends unsolicited temperature and humidity reports from the root endpoint while Home Assistant's exposed values were associated with different endpoints, so incoming reports did not update the corresponding entities.

Must also account for the later no-report state after reinclusion: the interview log showed that the group-1 lifeline association could not be assigned, preventing unsolicited reports from reaching the controller.
The final fix must be an updated Z-Wave JS add-on or driver build containing the ST814 compatibility and association-handling corrections, followed by a device re-interview.
Must not present manual refresh, endpoint-1-only mapping, the earlier driver update alone, or removing and re-adding the device as the complete fix; each was incomplete or failed in the thread.
Must ask the user to verify that both temperature and humidity update on a build containing the corrections before treating the issue as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Home Assistant power user familiar with integrations, add-ons, entity services, Z-Wave interviews, device parameters, and collecting logs, but uncertain about low-level driver configuration and where some diagnostic controls are located in the UI.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite and cooperative; gives concise status updates, corrects earlier observations after retesting, asks for step-by-step UI guidance when needed, and is willing to wait for battery-device wakeups and test updated add-ons.
